title: Hundreds of Thousands Protest Across France in Third Weekend of Cost-of-Living Marches
dek: The government estimated 320,000 people demonstrated nationwide on Saturday, fewer than the previous two weekends, as about 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Protesters with a union balloon at a demonstration in Paris (2016 file photo)

keyPoints: France's government estimated that 320,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday, according to AP, down from 410,000 the previous weekend and more than 500,000 on Oct. 17.
About 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed, and Paris marches were moved to the capital's edge, AP reported.
Authorities reported about 300 arrests nationwide by Saturday afternoon, down from 800 at the same point a week earlier, AP reported.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had warned of a "very high risk of public disorder" on Oct. 31, France 24 reported.
body:
Hundreds of thousands of mostly young people marched across France on Saturday in a third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, according to the Associated Press.

## Numbers and policing

The French government estimated that 320,000 people took part nationwide, AP reported, fewer than the 410,000 it counted on Oct. 24 and the more than 500,000 on Oct. 17, when protests turned into some of France's worst rioting in years. Organizers' estimates were much higher, AP noted.

About 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed. In Paris, the main march was routed outside the city centre after a last-minute court battle, the Interior Ministry said; 70,000 people were estimated to have joined it, down from 110,000 the previous Saturday, according to the New York Times.

## Warnings before the day

On Thursday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a "very high risk of public disorder" on Oct. 31 and said demonstrations would not be allowed in city centres. He also said authorities had found social media calls for Halloween gatherings described as a "revolution", and that those gatherings would be banned, France 24 reported.

## Background to the protests

The marches follow mass protests on Oct. 17 that turned into some of France's worst rioting in years, with looting and clashes, according to France 24. Police had arrested thousands of people after the riots and looting that marred the largely peaceful marches on the two Saturdays before Saturday's protest, AP reported. France has faced a debate over rising living costs and inequality, and the protests have drawn a growing number of students.

## What marchers want

AP described a mix of grievances, with high school students, climate activists and union members carrying separate banners. Organisers and marchers have cited rising living costs and inequality. Youth-led demonstrations were also reported in Germany and Italy, AP said.

A reported 300 arrests by Saturday afternoon compared with 800 at the same point last week, AP reported. This story will be updated if the government releases a final tally or if there are further disturbances.
